note: CKEditor Div Manager is a pure CKEditor 5 JS plugin with no PHP, no config schema, no permissions, no Drush, no configure route. Its ckeditor5.yml registers toolbar item 'DivManager' (label 'Div Manager') and grants <div> / <div class="simple-box-description">. It is enabled per text format by adding 'DivManager' to editor.editor.<format> settings.toolbar.items (editor must be ckeditor5). filter_html must allow <div> for the markup to survive. Medium/hard cases are grounded in real editor.editor and filter.format config: introspection reads which format has DivManager in its toolbar; execution adds DivManager to a toolbar and permits the <div> tag in filter_html.

evals.prompt: What does the Drupal contrib module ckeditor_div_manager add to CKEditor 5, and what HTML element can an editor insert with it? Name the toolbar button/item.
evals.expected_output: It adds a CKEditor 5 toolbar button whose toolbar item id is 'DivManager' (label 'Div Manager'). Clicking it opens a pop-up to insert a <div> container, optionally with class/id/title/lang/style attributes.

evals.prompt: How do I enable the ckeditor_div_manager Div Manager button on a specific Drupal text format, and what does the 'Limit allowed HTML tags' (filter_html) filter need to permit for it to work?
evals.expected_output: Edit the text format (Text formats and editors), which must use a CKEditor 5 editor, and drag Div Manager into the active toolbar (adds 'DivManager' to editor.editor.<format> settings.toolbar.items). If filter_html is on, allow at least <div> (and <div class id title> to keep the extra attributes).

evals.prompt: Which Drupal core module does ckeditor_div_manager depend on, and is it a PHP-heavy module or a JavaScript editor plugin?
evals.expected_output: It depends on the CKEditor 5 core module (drupal:ckeditor5). It is a pure CKEditor 5 JavaScript plugin integration - no PHP, no config schema, no permissions, no Drush. (It also carries a legacy Composer requirement on the CKEditor 4 div library group, unused by the 3.0.x build.)

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site there are two text formats, cdm_on and cdm_off. Exactly one of them has the ckeditor_div_manager 'Div Manager' button enabled in its CKEditor 5 toolbar. Inspect the live editor configuration and state which format has it.
evals.expected_output: cdm_on has it: editor.editor.cdm_on settings.toolbar.items contains 'DivManager', while cdm_off's toolbar does not.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site the text format cdm_known uses CKEditor 5. Inspect its live editor configuration and report whether the ckeditor_div_manager button is in its toolbar and the exact toolbar item id used.
evals.expected_output: Yes - editor.editor.cdm_known settings.toolbar.items is [heading, bold, DivManager, link], so the Div Manager button is enabled and its toolbar item id is 'DivManager'.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site the text format cdm_task uses a CKEditor 5 editor but does not yet offer the ckeditor_div_manager button. Add the Div Manager button to cdm_task's CKEditor 5 toolbar and apply the change to the live site.
evals.expected_output: editor.editor.cdm_task settings.toolbar.items now contains 'DivManager' (append 'DivManager' to the toolbar items and save the editor entity, or drag it in via the Text formats UI).

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site the text format cdm_filter has the ckeditor_div_manager Div Manager button in its CKEditor 5 toolbar, but its 'Limit allowed HTML tags' (filter_html) filter strips out <div> tags. Update the format so the filter permits the <div> tag, and apply the change to the live site.
evals.expected_output: The filter_html allowed_html string on filter.format.cdm_filter now includes a <div> tag (e.g. add '<div class id title>' to allowed_html and save the format).
